language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, my name is Leander! Meet my friend, Tim! Today, we'll explore this ancient Greek theatre.
Look at these statues behind us – how rustic and old they look.
These statues have been standing outside and have been weathered by the sun, rain, and storms. That's what's changed their appearance over the years.
My chemistry teacher also talked about different types of changes. And, I need to complete an assignment about substances as well.
Well I can help you with that, but first let's look around this huge theatre!
How about we revise the Chemistry lessons while exploring this place?
That's a great idea! Do you also want to join? Let's go!

Let's talk about different types of substances. A substance which can be easily dissolved in liquid, especially water, is known as a soluble substance.
Yes! For example, sugar completely dissolves in water.
Look, I see some items on this table. Can you help me identify the items that are soluble in water?

Thanks for helping me!
I'm so hungry! I'm so glad my mom prepared this food basket for us.
There is so much food in here! How about we dig out the goodies and figure out if they are soluble or insoluble?

Sure! Insoluble substances do not dissolve completely in a liquid, especially water. For example, sand is insoluble in water. Even after you stir the mixture of sand and water well, the sand will eventually settle down.
Let’s now pick out the items from the basket. Can you help me identify the items that are soluble and insoluble in water?

Did you know that some of the changes we see around us are reversible, while others are irreversible? I can't recall the difference between the two types. Tim, do you know what is a reversible change?

A reversible change is a change that can be undone or reversed. For example, you can freeze orange juice to make an ice lolly. However, this change is reversible as you can heat the ice lolly to convert it back into orange juice.
I got it! Hey, I have some pictures here. Can you help me select the pictures that depict a reversible change?

I think I can now take a guess at what an irreversible change is. A change is called irreversible if it cannot be undone or reversed.
Right, Leander! For example, you cannot change a cookie back into its ingredients again. Therefore, the process of baking cookies is an irreversible change.
Thanks, Tim.
